views.title: Records come from Raptor
views.text:
judge-jev MUST obtain records through Raptor's query interface.
judge-jev MUST NOT parse record Markdown itself.
judge-jev MUST NOT run SQL (Structured Query Language) against the record
store itself.

obligations.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. How many independent obligations does this statement impose?

term.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. Is every term in this statement common usage, defined in this record, or defined in a linked record?

criteria.yes: Every term is common usage, defined in this record, or defined in a linked record.
criteria.no: At least one term is none of these.

checkable.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. Can a tester decide whether this statement holds?

criteria.yes: Yes, by a test, a command run, or reading files.

d_term_kind.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What kind of term in this statement is unclear?

criteria.none: Every term is common usage or defined in the record.

joined_by.instructions: `item.text` is JSON: `statement` is one MUST or MUST NOT statement of the requirement record in `record`. Judge only `statement`; use `record` as context. What joins its obligations?

views.title: Keep the Jev core unchanged until its Rust replacement
views.text:
The Jev core keeps its architecture and contracts unchanged. It changes
only to fix a defect, or to replace its run log with the sc-observability
logger (REQ-JEV-0008).

tree.note: wave-1 wording approved by Rand Lee, 2026-11-08

context.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does its context name the problem and the forces behind the decision?

criteria.problem and forces: Names the problem and the forces or constraints that shaped the decision.
criteria.background only: Gives background but no problem. Fix: state the problem.
criteria.missing: No context in substance. Fix: add the problem and its forces.

alternatives.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does it name the alternatives considered?

criteria.named with reasons rejected: Names alternatives and why each was rejected.
criteria.named only: Names alternatives without why they were rejected. Fix: add why rejected.
criteria.none: Names no alternative. Fix: add alternatives.

consequences.instructions: `item.text` is one architecture decision record as JSON. Does it name the decision's consequences?

criteria.positive only: Names only benefits. Fix: add the costs.
criteria.missing: Names no consequence. Fix: add benefits and costs.
